pages.title: Property Condition & Compliance

questions.question: Is the property built as per the development authority’s sanctioned building plan?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Planned Area
In planned/authority areas, lenders check whether construction follows the approved layout and sanctioned plan from DDA/MHADA/BDA/HUDA or similar authority.
💡 Tip: Not fully compliant does not mean rejection — some NBFCs fund deviated properties at different terms.

options.label: Yes — fully as per approved plan
Minor deviations from approved plan
options.helperText: Small differences like balcony enclosure, staircase variation

options.label: Major deviations or no approved plan

condition.then: Properties with deviations from approved plan have fewer lender options. Select NBFCs may still process at adjusted terms.

questions.question: Has the land been formally converted from agricultural to residential use (NA conversion)?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Converted Land
Banks require confirmed NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion before financing any property on converted land. Without this, the property is treated as agricultural — which no bank will finance.

options.label: Yes — NA order received and registered

condition.then: NA conversion is still pending -- loan processing will be on hold until conversion is complete. High-risk status for lenders.
Non-NA land -- ineligible for financing. The land must be converted from agricultural use before any lender can process this loan.

questions.question: Is the property within municipal limits with valid municipal records?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Municipal Area
For properties in old municipal/city areas, lenders verify municipal records, property tax, and building permission history.

options.label: Yes — proper municipal records and building permission
Municipal area but original plan has deviations
options.helperText: Extra floor, balcony extension, unauthorized room addition

options.label: No formal building permission or municipal records

condition.then: Minor deviations in municipal areas are common. Some banks and most NBFCs can still process with adjusted valuation.

questions.question: Is the colony officially recognised or regularized by the government?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Local Colony
Properties in village/panchayat areas are evaluated based on whether the colony or layout has been officially recognized. Regularized colonies have more lender options.

options.label: Yes — colony is regularized with proper records

condition.then: Non-regularized colony properties are not accepted by banks. Specialized housing finance companies (Aavas, Grihashakti) may consider at higher interest rates and lower loan-to-value ratios.

questions.question: Is the property in a government-authorized area and built as per approved plan?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance Status
This determines which lenders (banks vs NBFCs) can process the application.
💡 Tip: Not fully compliant does not mean rejection — some NBFCs fund non-authorized or deviated properties at different terms.

options.label: Yes — authorized area, as per approved plan
Authorized area, but not as per plan

condition.then: Properties that are not fully compliant may still be eligible for funding through select NBFCs. Fewer lenders will appear in the results, but options are available.

questions.question: Has the building received its OC (Occupancy Certificate) / CC (Completion Certificate)?
questions.description:
📋 OC / CC Status
Most banks require OC/CC for processing. Without OC, lenders may consider the property legally incomplete.

questions.question: Was the house built with a sanctioned building plan from the local authority?
questions.description:
🏛️ Building Plan Approval
For independent houses, lenders check whether construction followed a plan sanctioned by the local authority.

questions.question: Has the authority granted possession (OC/CC issued)?
questions.description:
📋 Authority Possession Status
This refers to official government certification — not possession offered directly by the builder.

questions.question: Is the project registered under RERA?
questions.description:
🏢 RERA Registration
RERA registration is mandatory for projects over 500 sq.m. Banks verify RERA number before sanctioning loans for under-construction properties.

condition.then: Banks will not finance under-construction projects without RERA registration. Verify with the builder.

questions.question: What is the current status of the NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion order?
questions.description:
📜 NA Conversion Status
The NA order from the District Collector’s office is the key document proving land use has been changed from agricultural to residential.

options.label: Already in residential zone (no conversion needed)

condition.then: Without NA conversion, no lender can process this loan. The conversion process typically takes 2-6 months.

questions.question: What is the zone classification of this land?
questions.description:
🗺️ Zone Classification
Zone classification determines permissible construction type. Lenders prefer residential or mixed-use zones.

condition.then: Commercial-zoned property: Some lenders may restrict residential loans on commercial-zoned land. Verify lender policy.

questions.question: Is the municipal/property tax being paid regularly?
questions.description:
💰 Municipal Tax Status
Regular tax payment history proves the property is recognized by the municipal body — an important signal for lenders.

options.label: Yes — paid regularly and up to date
Paid but with gaps or arrears

condition.then: Properties without municipal tax records are difficult to finance. Clearing arrears and obtaining tax receipts is recommended before applying.

questions.question: Are there any unauthorized additions or modifications to the property?
questions.description:
🚧 Unauthorized Additions
Extra floors, room additions, or balcony enclosures without permission are common in older areas. The extent affects lender decisions and valuation.

options.label: Minor additions (balcony enclosure, extra room)
options.helperText: Small changes that don't alter the building footprint significantly

condition.then: Major unauthorized construction significantly reduces lender options. Banks will likely reject; select NBFCs may consider at lower LTV and higher rates.

questions.question: What is the status of revenue records for this property?
questions.description:
📑 Revenue Records
Revenue records (7/12 extract in Maharashtra, Khata in Karnataka, Patta in Tamil Nadu, Jamabandi in Rajasthan/Punjab) are the primary proof of land ownership in village/panchayat areas.

options.label: Available and up to date
options.helperText: 7/12, Khata, Patta, RTC — whichever applies in your state

options.label: Available but not updated recently
options.helperText: Records exist but mutation or name transfer pending

condition.then: Properties without revenue records are extremely difficult to finance. Even specialized NBFCs require some form of ownership documentation.

questions.question: Has this colony/layout been regularized by the government?
questions.description:
🏘️ Colony Regularization
Many villages and panchayat areas have colonies that were developed informally but later regularized by state government orders. Regularized colonies are accepted by more lenders.

questions.question: Has the Gram Panchayat issued permission for this construction?
questions.description:
🏡 Gram Panchayat Permission
In panchayat areas, the Gram Panchayat is the local authority that grants building permission. This serves as proof of authorized construction.

questions.question: What is the current construction progress?
questions.description:
🏗️ Construction Progress
The percentage of construction completed helps assess project maturity and risk timeline.

questions.question: When is the project expected to be completed?
questions.description:
📅 Expected Completion
Expected completion date helps determine loan tenure and disbursement schedule.

questions.question: What is the builder's reputation for on-time delivery?
questions.description:
⭐ Builder Track Record
Builder's history of timely delivery affects project completion risk and loan disbursement strategy.

options.label: Unknown - First time buyer / new builder

questions.question: Are all required project approvals in place?
questions.description:
✅ Project Approvals
Approvals (layout approval, environmental clearance, building permission) affect project legitimacy and lender acceptance.

questions.question: Who is selling the property?
questions.description:
👤 Seller Identity
The seller's ownership type affects title verification complexity and documentation requirements.
💡 Endorsement Reminder: For resale via endorsement, the seller is typically the builder or their nominee.

condition.then: Inherited properties require succession certificate or legal heir certificate. Title chain verification will be more thorough.
POA-based sales require registered power of attorney. Most banks require the POA to be specifically for property sale, not a general POA.

questions.question: Is the power of attorney registered?
questions.description:
📋 POA Registration
Registered POA (with sub-registrar) is mandatory for property transactions. Unregistered or notarized-only POA is not accepted by any major lender.

condition.then: Unregistered POA is not accepted by any major lender for property transactions. This is a deal-breaker for financing.
POA registration status must be verified before loan processing. Ask seller for the registered POA document.

questions.question: How did the seller acquire this property?
questions.description:
📑 Acquisition Method
The way the seller acquired the property determines the title chain complexity and documentation requirements for the loan.

options.label: Agreement to Sell + POA (no registered sale deed)

condition.then: Inherited property requires succession/legal heir certificate and consent of all legal heirs. Extra documentation and longer processing.
Gift deed properties may have restricted transfer clauses. Lenders verify gift deed registration and donor's title before approval.
Government-allotted properties may have transfer restrictions or cooling periods. Original allotment letter and NOC from authority required.

After the Supreme Court ruling (Suraj Lamp & Industries, 2012), property transfer via Agreement to Sell + POA + Will + Revenue Receipt is not legally valid. No major bank will finance such deals. Only select NBFCs in certain areas may have workarounds.

questions.question: Are both seller and buyer willing to get the property registered first?
questions.description:
📝 Registration Recommendation
The seller must register the property via a proper sale deed. Registration will be at the consideration rate (Agreement to Sell value or circle/guideline rate, whichever is higher). Advise the DSA to explain this to both parties.

options.label: Yes — both parties agree to register first, then apply for loan
No — seller/buyer not willing to register

condition.then: Once the property is registered, this becomes a normal resale purchase. The case can proceed.
Without registration, no major bank will finance this deal. Only select NBFCs in certain areas may have workarounds.

questions.description: Required if property has an existing loan — confirms previous lender will clear the lien.

questions.question: Is the ownership chain (title chain) clear and complete?
questions.description:
🔗 Title Chain Verification
Lenders verify the ownership chain for at least 13–30 years. Each transfer must be properly documented with registered sale deeds. Gaps in the chain can cause loan rejection.

options.label: Some gaps exist but can be resolved
options.helperText: Missing link deed, unregistered partition, etc.

condition.then: Unclear title chain is a primary reason for loan rejection. A legal opinion from a bank-empaneled advocate is recommended before proceeding.

questions.question: Has the Encumbrance Certificate (EC) been obtained and verified?
questions.description:
🔍 Encumbrance Certificate
The EC from the Sub-Registrar’s office proves the property is free from mortgages, liens, and legal claims. Banks typically require 13–30 years of EC.

options.label: Existing liens or mortgages on property

condition.then: Existing encumbrances must be cleared before a new loan can be sanctioned. For BT cases, the existing lien will be cleared as part of the balance transfer.

questions.question: Is this property inherited? If so, is the succession properly documented?
questions.description:
🏠 Succession Status
For inherited properties, lenders require succession certificate, legal heir certificate, probate of will, or partition deed — depending on how the property was inherited.

options.label: Inherited — succession documents complete
options.helperText: Succession certificate, will probate, or mutation done

condition.then: Incomplete succession documentation will delay or prevent loan processing. Succession certificate or mutation must be completed first.

questions.question: Is the property mutation (name transfer in revenue records) up to date?
questions.description:
📝 Revenue Record Mutation
Mutation (Dakhil Kharij) reflects the current owner’s name in government revenue records. Lenders verify this to confirm the seller’s right to sell.

options.label: Yes — mutation done, records reflect current owner
Not mutated — records show previous owner

condition.then: Revenue records not showing the current owner can delay or block loan processing. Mutation is typically required before disbursement.
